name: backlog
//changelogVocabulary: Consumed by the `version` executor (tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/version/impl.js, `scrubGeneratedChangelog`): a path (relative to this project root) to a module exporting `scrubChangelog(text)`, applied to the GENERATED CHANGELOG.md after `nx release changelog` writes it. The changelog is a projection of git commit subjects, so a commit that REMOVES a banned term names it — which this package's own vocabulary-gate then scans. Fixing it at the generator keeps the shipped changelog clean while the gate keeps scanning it in full (no exemption). The same module is the SINGLE SOURCE both gates import (tools/gate/vocabulary-gate.mjs, scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs), so the term list cannot drift. Declared for @adhd/backlog ONLY — other packages whose changelogs legitimately name such terms as external dependencies are deliberately left untouched.

build.//: OVERRIDE of the @nx/vite-inferred `build` so ONE target emits BOTH `dist/api.d.ts` (vite/dts) and `dist/api.ir.json` (the bake-at-build IR artifact, design doc Revision 3). The second command runs the built bin's hidden `ir-artifact` subcommand, which extracts the just-written `api.d.ts` and writes the artifact beside it in the SAME `dist/`. A SEPARATE target would have to declare the same `{projectRoot}/dist` output and could clobber this one's cache snapshot; keeping both in one target makes `dist/` a single atomic output. Mirrors the inferred target otherwise: `executor: nx:run-commands` + `cwd: {projectRoot}` + `vite build` (main's inferred `cwd` was the literal `entrypoint/backlog`; `{projectRoot}` is the equivalent, path-independent form), `cache: true`, `outputs: [{projectRoot}/dist]`, `dependsOn: [^build, typecheck]`, `inputs: [production, ^production]` — `typecheck` is kept because the artifact step runs the built bin, so a type error must fail the build before it does. `parallel: false` is REQUIRED: the artifact command depends on `vite build` having finished writing `api.d.ts`.

test.//: Override of the inferred `test` target (dependsOn only; executor/cache/outputs come from inference — the @nx/vitest plugin replaces main's removed `@nx/vite:test` executor, and its coverage output matches vite.config.ts's reportsDirectory, which main's explicit output did not). Backlog's OWN `build` + `assets` are load-bearing: the remaining default-lane specs (e.g. src/mcp-discoverability-real-ops.spec.ts reads dist/api.d.ts) and the vocabulary-gate pack the real built dist/, and `assets` (BUG-013 FIX A) is what copies dist/skill/SKILL.md in. `vocabulary-gate` (C-22) makes both vocabulary acceptance gates run on every `nx affected -t test`. `lint`/`^build` mirror the workspace `test` targetDefaults, which an explicit dependsOn otherwise replaces.

e2e.//: On-demand RESOURCE lane (backlog-e2e-separation): the 33 `src/**/*.e2e.ts` suites extracted out of `test` — real subprocess spawns, the real fastembed model, real bound-port HTTP/MCP servers, and the CPU/mem/disk/io hogs — each paired 1:1 with a cheap `*.spec.ts` stub left in the default lane (see the stub `Resource lane:` tags and vitest.e2e.config.ts). REACHABILITY GUARD: this target is deliberately unreachable from `nx affected` and from a bare `test` run — it appears in NO target's `dependsOn` and is deliberately absent from `nx.json` `targetDefaults`, so ONLY an explicit `nx run backlog:e2e` (or `nx run-many -t e2e`) runs it. Never add it to `test.dependsOn`. `dependsOn:["build"]` is the ONLY dependency the suites need: every one either spawns the built `dist/index.js` or loads the real model/store/server, and the three published-layout/install-skill suites that read `dist/skill/SKILL.md` are satisfied by `build` ALONE — vite.config.ts's copySkillDirPlugin writes it on a bare `nx build backlog` (verified 2026-09-24: dist/skill/SKILL.md present after build, dist/README.md absent) — so `assets` and `vocabulary-gate` are NOT dependencies. No `outputs` declared: a dist-shaped output would let this target's cache restore clobber `build`'s dist/, and coverage is opt-in. TARGET NAME (backlog-e2e-separation review): the lane deliberately KEEPS the name `e2e` for repo-wide consistency — the 12 sibling apigen packages (apigen-cli, -core-client, -engine-conformance, -engine-runtime, -plugin-api-express, -plugin-api-fastify, -plugin-cli-output, -plugin-java-javalin, -plugin-mcp, -plugin-py-flask, -plugin-py-grpc, python-env) name their identical resource lane `e2e` across 5 branches, so renaming only this one would split the same concept into two names. LATENT COLLISION (accepted, documented): `nx.json`'s @nx/cypress/plugin reserves `targetName: "e2e"` (and `ciTargetName: "e2e-ci"`), so IF a cypress project is ever added (none exists today — zero cypress.config.*, zero *.cy.*) a `nx run-many -t e2e` would sweep both semantics. A global `targetDefaults.e2e` MUST NEVER be added to cross-wire them: `targetDefaults` is keyed by target NAME only (nx-schema.json `targetDefaults.additionalProperties`, no project filter), so it cannot be scoped to this project — the project-scoped home for every default here IS this `targets.e2e` block, which is why the full config lives inline above rather than in nx.json. INVARIANT: never add this target to `test.dependsOn` and never add a global `targetDefaults.e2e`. `passWithNoTests` is deliberately ABSENT so a mis-collected lane (a broken glob, a config/file move) fails loudly instead of exiting green on zero collected files (AGENTS.md §7: never make it quietly skip).

vocabulary-gate.//: C-22: both vocabulary acceptance gates, as one Nx task. `tools/gate/vocabulary-gate.mjs` scans src/ (code AND text assets such as src/write/CONTRACT.md) plus the package's top-level markdown (SPEC/DESIGN/DATA_MODEL/RAG-SPEC/README/CHANGELOG); `scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs` npm-packs the REAL artifact (package.json `files`: dist + CHANGELOG.md + skill) and scans the tarball — the only scan that catches a banned token reaching a consumer through dist/*.d.ts, which reproduces source doc comments verbatim and never appears in src/. Wired into test.dependsOn so the PR workflows' `nx affected -t test` runs it on every PR touching this package. dependsOn build+assets so the packed artifact is the real shipped one, never a stale dist/. cache:true mirrors the verify-dist-load convention — deterministic given `inputs: ["default"]`: a src/doc change re-runs it, and a dist/ change re-runs it too because nx folds the build/assets dependency task hashes into this task's hash, so dist/ (a dependency OUTPUT, not an input) needs no explicit input entry. NOTE: check-vocabulary.mjs takes NO path arg here deliberately — cwd is already {projectRoot} and the script defaults to process.cwd(); passing {projectRoot} again double-prefixes the path, npm pack spawns with a nonexistent cwd, and the failure surfaces as the misleading 'spawnSync npm ENOENT' (verified while authoring this target). backlog-e2e-separation review (HIGH finding): two MORE static policy gates run here, so they are default-running and never depend on the resource `e2e` lane — `tools/gate/embedding-usage-gate.mjs` censuses the real-vs-fake embedding policy across BOTH `*.spec.ts` and `*.e2e.ts` (its live assertion had been left in the resource-only `vocabulary-gate.e2e.ts`, with no Nx target at all), and `tools/gate/spawn-isolation-gate.mjs` is the static/parsing half of the spawn-isolation guard (every `spawn(process.execPath, [DIST_INDEX, …]` site must import an isolation helper), which had lost its only default-running executor when `spawn-isolated-bin.e2e.ts` moved to the resource lane. Both are pure reads/regexes with no child spawn and no model load, so they belong in the fast lane; do NOT move either back into an e2e suite.

metadata.description: Runs the package's static policy gates: the two vocabulary acceptance gates (src-tree scan + packed-tarball scan) — non-zero exit on any banned humanId/migration/sqlite reference anywhere, and on v1/v2 outside generated bundles — plus the embedding-usage census (real-vs-fake) and the spawn-isolation guard. All four are cheap static reads; runs on every PR touching the package via test.dependsOn.

assets.//: BUG-013 FIX A hardening (original): the globally-inferred @adhd/nx-assets:copy target (tools/nx-plugins/assets/plugin.js) declares NO `outputs` at all, so a later cache HIT on THIS project's `build` target (whose own declared `outputs` is the whole `dist/` dir) silently restores build's own cached dist/ SNAPSHOT — taken before `assets` ever ran — wiping whatever `assets` had already copied in (dist/skill/, dist/README.md, dist/CHANGELOG.md), with no re-copy on `assets`'s own subsequent cache hit (nothing declared to restore). Declaring explicit `outputs`/`inputs` here was meant to fix that. Scoped to backlog only — the SAME underlying gap (already tracked as BUG-BUILD-ASSETS-CACHE-STALE-AFTER-CLEAN-001, tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/manifest) affects every OTHER `assets`-consuming project too, worked around there only for the publish/manifest path.
assets.//bug-026: BUG-026 FIX: the original fix above set `outputs: ["{projectRoot}/dist"]` — the WHOLE directory, the exact same literal path `build`'s own outputs (`{options.outputPath}`) claims. nx's cache restore for a directory-shaped output does `remove(dir); copy(cachedDir, dir)` (node_modules/nx/src/tasks-runner/cache.js `copyFilesFromCache`) — a full SWAP, not a merge. `test`'s dependsOn is `["^build", "build", "assets", "vocabulary-gate"]` (vocabulary-gate added C-22; it depends on build+assets itself and owns no dist outputs, so it does not participate in the swap ordering): when only `build`'s inputs change (source fix, cache MISS -> fresh rebuild) while `assets`'s own inputs (README/CHANGELOG/skill/package.json) don't (cache HIT), nx restores `assets`'s STALE recorded snapshot of the ENTIRE dist dir over the freshly-built one, silently reverting `dist/index.js` to whatever it was when `assets` last ran (measured 2026-08-18: a 4-day-stale artifact missing BUG-020's fix). FIX: scope `outputs` to ONLY the files this target's own executor (tools/nx-plugins/assets/executors/copy/impl.js) actually writes — never the bare shared `dist` directory `build` also owns. Regression test: tools/nx-plugins/build/bug-026-assets-output-scope.spec.mjs (reads this exact config live).

serve.//: web UI prototype: spawns the real built CLI (`serve --transport http`) + a static/proxy web server (tools/run-web-ui.mjs) and owns both lifecycles. `nx serve backlog` then `open http://127.0.0.1:4173/`. Pass-through flags (e.g. `--sandbox` for an isolated store) go after `--`: `npx nx serve backlog -- --sandbox`. Long-lived dev process — never cacheable.
